claims.explanation: WAY-170523 is annotated as an MMP13 inhibitor, but its selective killing pattern and transcriptional signature (hypoxia/HIF1A target genes ALDOC, BNIP3, BNIP3L, PDGFA, DDIT4, HMOX1; caspase/BCL-related similarity) suggest that sensitivity is driven by dependence on hypoxia/oxidative-stress and apoptotic signaling rather than MMP13 itself. TP53 loss and PI3K/PTEN pathway activation are the most consistent genomic correlates of sensitivity, while intact apoptotic/BCL-2 signaling and EGFR/BRAF-driven lineages are protective.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in nearly all selectively killed lines and absent in most protected lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling that is associated with the drug's apoptotic signature
PIK3CA mutation observed in multiple sensitive lines and links to PI3K pathway dependence
NF1 loss causes RAS/MAPK hyperactivation and appears enriched in sensitive lines
KRAS mutation present in several sensitive lines including pancreatic and neuroblastoma
BNIP3 is strongly upregulated in the virtual cell response, indicating hypoxia/apoptotic priming
BNIP3L upregulation in the virtual cell response supports a hypoxia-induced apoptotic mechanism
DDIT4 upregulation indicates mTOR inhibition and stress-response activation in responsive lines
HMOX1 upregulation suggests oxidative-stress response contributing to sensitivity
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines appear in both sensitive and protected groups, but EGFR-driven survival signaling may blunt the drug's effect
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are predominantly in the least-affected group
MMP13 is the annotated target; high expression may indicate dependence on the inhibited protease and thus reduced sensitivity if the drug is a weak inhibitor
